newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Dozens freed, many still stuck in Russian tunnel.
newsitem.headline: Dozens freed, many still stuck in Russian tunnel.

text.p: Several dozen people and their vehicles were freed on Sunday after being trapped for days by avalanches in a tunnel in southern Russia but many more remained captive, Interfax news agency said.
It said rescue workers had cleared away some 19 kilometres of snow blocking a mountainous highway that links Russia's North Ossetia region with the breakaway Georgian province of South Ossetia.
But much of the highway, including the four km (2.5 mile) Roksky tunnel that cuts through the Caucasus mountain range, remains heavily blocked by snow, Interfax said.
As many as 300 people may still be trapped inside the tunnel and more avalanches and rockfalls are expected in the area as snow continues to fall, Itar-Tass news agency said.
On Saturday agencies had reported that only 80 people were trapped along the entire highway. They also said at least two people had died in the area.

Rescue teams and doctors, entering the tunnel by foot, have managed to deliver food, medicine and warm clothing. Some of the motorists trapped have refused to budge in case their cars are stolen or looted, agencies said.
Tass said the severe weather barred any evacuation of motorists by helicopter and officials fear a build-up of exhaust fumes in the tunnel could become a health hazard for those still trapped.
